content:
anya: Heads-up: onboarding sampleapp locked up during prefetch. Token refresh fired mid-window and all prefetch workers blocked.

anya: Repro: prefetchConcurrency=3, tokenTTL=15s, tokenRefreshSync=true. Observed: prefetch workers waiting on auth mutex -> pages stop streaming.

sam: That config sounds like it will deadlock if refresh is sync. We fixed similar in Go; JS might still use a global lock.

jing: Can you paste minimal logs?

anya: logs: 
```
prefetch worker[1]: fetch page=2 waiting on auth refresh
auth: refresh started (sync)
prefetch worker[2]: blocked
http client: queued 401 retries
```

tyler: Quick workaround: set tokenRefreshSync=false so refresh is async. Prefetch will continue and failed requests are retried.

anya: Async avoids the stall but causes a small bump in 401 retries (~1%). Not ideal for docs.

sam: Proposal: SDK changes: (1) snapshot token per batch so prefetchers don't block, (2) run refresh async without holding prefetch lock, (3) add config allowOptimisticPrefetch + metric prefetch.auth_retries.

jing: Agree. Also add tiny jitter to prefetch start to avoid coordinated expiry. Need parity across JS/Go.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy started for branch "prefetch-optimistic-2026" (id d-7982).

anya: I'll open a PR with tests that simulate mid-window expiry and a deterministic clock for jitter. I'll also update quickstart to recommend tokenRefreshSync=false until this lands.

sam: Nice. Keep the optimistic prefetch opt-in until telemetry looks good.
